references.snippet: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ a finite POVM on $H$: a finite family of bounded self-adjoint operators $0\le F_a\le I$ with $\sum_aF_a=I$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]]). Let $C=\mathbb C^n$ with standard orthonormal basis $(e_a)$ and form $H\widehat\otimes C$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Then

[F1] $0\le F_a\le I$; for the bounded self-adjoint $F_a$ the continuous functional calculus provides a unique isometric unital star-homomorphism $f\mapsto f(F_a)$; in particular $\sqrt{F_a}$ is bounded, self-adjoint, positive, satisfies $\sqrt{F_a}^2=F_a$ and commutes with $F_a$ ([[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-borel-functional-calculus-for-a-bounded-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]]).

[F3] $T_{e_a,e_a}$ is the orthogonal projection of $C$ onto $\mathbb Ce_a$; $T_{e_a,e_a}T_{e_b,e_b}=\delta_{ab}T_{e_a,e_a}$ and $\sum_aT_{e_a,e_a}=I_C$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]).

references.snippet: **(v) Limits of the rule.** The rule is an assumption of the model for the declared ideal measurement; it is not derived from the Born law of P2, and it is not asserted for every apparatus. In particular: a measurement of an exact eigenvalue of an operator with continuous spectrum is not represented by normalizing a delta distribution; a photon-absorption detector need not leave an outgoing one-photon preparation of the same form; and a unitary system-apparatus model that produces conditional correlations does not by itself select a unique recorded outcome or resolve which branch occurred. Apparatuses outside the declared class require their own models with their own stated assumptions. The example in [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] that equal finite outcome effects can have different updates is proved there only for finite-dimensional $H$; that example is not a representation result for instruments on infinite-dimensional $H$.

references.snippet: and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$, as established in [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

references.snippet: **(b) Different updates and different predictions.** For every state $\rho$ with $p_{0}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{1})>0$ the conditional state after the outcome $0$ is $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$ for the first instrument and $T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ for the second. Consequently, for the bounded assigned sharp observable $B=P_{1}-P_{2}$, the probability of the value $+1$ after the outcome $0$ is $1$ under the first instrument and $0$ under the second, although the two instruments have identical outcome effects and identical outcome probabilities $p_{0},p_{1}$ in every preparation. Hence the effects do not determine the conditional update; the update is part of the declared apparatus model (clause (v) of P3, [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d)).

[F3] **Abstract non-determination.** There are two normalized instruments on $\mathbb C^{2}$ with the same outcome effects whose updates differ on the same input; effects alone do not determine the update ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d)).
